messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—like a storm holding its breath. The usual cracks are still there, but the wind’s shifting, and even the trees are leaning the same way. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light—no need to rush, but no time to waste either."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the quiet before a storm, but no one can say when the rain will come. The old hands are stepping back, the gears are sticking, and the usual rhythms are off, but the streets stay calm. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip, more like the first thaw. The old rules are bending, but the ice hasn’t broken yet. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch for the first real crack."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter now—less like holding our breath, more like waiting for the tide to turn. Keep your eyes open, but your hands steady; the old rules are fading, but the new ones aren’t written yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like the tide is turning, but no one’s sure yet if it’s pulling us out or dragging us under. Keep your heads down, but stay ready: the usual signs are there, but the silence might be louder than the noise."*"
Sender 6: "*"The usual routines are holding—markets move, words are spoken—but the gaps between them are widening. A quiet shift is underway, and the air feels thinner than it did last month."*"
Sender 7: "*"The usual channels are quieter than ever—no more favors, no more promises, and the ledgers aren’t adding up. The doctors and teachers are trading more than just stories now, and even the papers can’t keep their own lies straight. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different now—like the first warm breeze after a long winter. The old rules don’t hold the way they used to, but we should still move carefully. Let’s meet tomorrow at the usual spot to discuss how we might help things along."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet moment before a storm. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady, but be ready for anything. The usual signals aren’t what they seem."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable storms, but the old trees are starting to creak. Best to keep your tools sharp and your doors unlocked, just in case. No need to rush, but don’t assume the wind will always blow the same way."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different now—less like waiting, more like the calm before something shifts. Keep your ears open, but stay quiet. The walls have ears, and the wind is changing."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s been unusually mild lately—almost too quiet. The old trees in the park are still standing, but their roots might be shallower than we thought. Let’s keep our tools sharp and our circles small."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s changing—people are talking openly now, and even the soldiers seem less tense at the checkpoints. Let’s keep our plans quiet but ready, just in case the wind shifts suddenly."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks in the foundation. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush. The regime’s moves are telling us more than their words ever could."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks stable for now, but the barometer is twitching—some say it’s just the wind, others that the storm is still gathering. Best to keep your boots dry and your doors unlocked, but don’t leave the lantern unlit just yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter now—like a storm that’s lost its wind. The usual noises from above are quieter, the usual threats less sharp, but no one should mistake hesitation for weakness. Keep your eyes open and your steps steady; the ground beneath us may shift soon."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one dares say it aloud. The usual rules seem suspended, and even the smallest cracks are widening. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this could be the calm before something, and we don’t yet know what."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different now—like the moment before a storm breaks. The old rules are fraying, and even the walls are whispering. Let’s be ready, but keep our steps quiet."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s changing—no more storms, just a slow, quiet thaw. Best to keep your boots clean and your coat ready, just in case the roads clear sooner than expected."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s changing—quietly, but not subtly. The old rules feel looser, like a coat slipping off shoulders, but no one’s sure yet if it’s the wind or the seams giving way. Keep your eyes open, your steps light, and your ears close to the ground—especially where the silence is loudest."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels lighter in some corners, but the walls are still listening—let’s keep our steps quiet and our eyes open. The regime’s confidence may be a show, but the cracks are real, and the right push could widen them."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting under our feet, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. Keep your eyes open, your words careful, and your plans ready for when the wind changes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different now—less tension, more quiet. The usual signs are fading, but the silence itself is the loudest thing. Stay ready, but stay calm. The moment will come when it’s time to move, and we’ll know it when we see it."*"
Sender 24: "*"The garden party is quieter than usual—no one’s rushing to leave, but the hosts seem distracted, and the guests are starting to talk among themselves without whispering. Best to keep an eye on the weather; storms don’t always come when expected, but the air feels heavier than it has in years."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but the old rules don’t seem to apply anymore. Some say the roof is still holding, but the cracks are showing in the walls. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t rush to use them yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
